purpose: Research-only map of useful mathematical question morphologies drawn from teacher-accessible reference collections. Not an assessment bank.
notes: Seven CPM Tools courses confirmed from active course packages and the Algebra 1 root bank.
Sources are used only to study mathematical task architecture, legal parameters, representations, and progression. Do not copy copyrighted prompts, values, diagrams or answer choices.
Review & Preview remains restricted to each original CPM textbook lesson; external ideas cannot substitute for original R/P.
Canonical _question_structure question-family contracts remain authoritative; do not create duplicate families solely because the wording differs.
All entries must be mapped to current course Framework + exact Assessment Plan and independent answer/visual QA before use.
The saved prior DeltaMath question examples were found through conversation/project files, not confirmed in the shown Resources folder.

ideas.question_structure_idea: Given counted shapes, ask part-to-part versus part-to-whole; choose which ratio a statement represents.
Use ingredient quantities and servings to find an unknown quantity without supplying the equation.
Give a partly completed ratio table with a nonadjacent gap and have student infer the rule.
Supply an answer-neutral double number line and find a missing coordinate or unit rate.
Given bags/blocks on both pans, determine unknown content, then transition to equivalent equations.
ideas.notes: Must render accurate balance model, not a verbal description.

ideas.question_structure_idea: Use a functional context to distinguish independent/dependent variables and correct a wrong claim.
Give two corresponding figures to calculate scale factor from first to second and reverse.
Determine corresponding edges when figures are scaled and rotated; optionally find the factor.
Provide part of an enlarged/reduced image and ask student to construct the remaining vertices.
difficulty_progression: combining rotation with scaling only if taught
ideas.notes: Student grid must not include completed target figure; use registered graph tool.

ideas.student_action: Reason backward with a multiplicative factor
ideas.question_structure_idea: Give source/output quantities and ask both unit scaling stages or a single multiplier.
Connect equivalent scale situations across picture, table, and equation without redundant calculation.
difficulty_progression: distractor that preserves one ratio only

ideas.question_structure_idea: Give enlarged/reduced figure and ask students to infer original dimensions or vertices.
Read a rate from meaningful coordinates and distinguish horizontal/vertical unit roles.
Use axis labels to determine a part-to-part ratio instead of reflexively saying y/x.

ideas.student_action: Build a graph from rate changes
ideas.question_structure_idea: Give starting condition and timed stages; construct a continuous piecewise linear graph.
ideas.notes: Use graph tool for blank student axes; completion shown only in solution view.

ideas.question_structure_idea: Given time graph, identify intervals of change, totals, and where a rate becomes zero.
Rotate equation morphology rather than coefficient-only swaps; include variables on both sides as appropriate.
Build and compare two contexts with actual differing rates and starting values.
One family per product, quotient, or power-of-power action; present equivalent products differently.
Require actual simplification, then ask rule name via selected response or matching.
difficulty_progression: combination of rules if lesson allows

ideas.question_structure_idea: Students construct equation from wording; no equation supplied in task.
Ensure true distribution where labeled, terms combined where labeled, and planned unique solutions.

ideas.student_action: Evaluate f and g for several inputs
ideas.question_structure_idea: Keep function definitions and notation in every variation rather than collapsing to arithmetic.
Use a mathematically correct blank generic rectangle to relate dimensions, partial areas, and polynomial product.
ideas.notes: Cells must be tall and blank; do not put underlines inside cells.

ideas.question_structure_idea: Ask for a missing corresponding side while requiring evidence of scale direction.
difficulty_progression: fractional scale with distracting side labels

ideas.question_structure_idea: Give only necessary original figure and partial image and let student complete with accurate proportions.
Provide conventional geometric marks and ask whether sufficient conditions exist.
Use vertex coordinates to test invariants after transformations rather than only plotting.

ideas.student_action: Find one quantity needed by another
ideas.question_structure_idea: Build true dependency chains such as infer unknown dimension then area, not unrelated subparts.
Show an incorrect mapping of corresponding sides and ask for a corrected one.
Vary degree, missing terms, negative outer parentheses and collection order.
Keep multiplication as task, vary factor degree and representation without reducing to mere sign swaps.
Construct cases where reciprocal, negative exponent and composition interact legitimately.
Given output, determine possible inputs and domain constraints; use function notation.

ideas.student_action: Distinguish algebraic simplification from excluded inputs
ideas.question_structure_idea: Vary factorable numerator/denominator and show cancellation not domain restoration.
Use irregularly sampled tables to distinguish first difference from constant ratio.
Move both directions: symbolic transformation to graph and graph to transformation parameters.
Use intervals and endpoint types explicitly; require student to graph or identify continuity features.

ideas.student_action: Match exact angle and geometric ratio
ideas.question_structure_idea: Compare unit-circle values to reference triangles and signed quadrants without trivial recall only.
Require student to identify equivalent equation forms and solve where domain permits.
Contrast canceled factors, vertical asymptotes, horizontal/slant behavior in actual functions.
Give intercepts, behavior or table data and ask for possible functions with validation.
difficulty_progression: create two distinct models with same features

qa_gates: Confirm exact CPM I-can and lesson fit
Match existing canonical family ID or specify new candidate family for review
Ensure sensible three-level progression when appropriate; no fixed family count
Choose variation axes beyond noun/number swaps for conceptual tasks
Generate student representation with canonical tools and no answer leakage
Verify every prompt and solution independently
For original CPM Review & Preview, keep original source stimulus and any essential diagram/example
Keep catalog separate from active banks until teacher approves
